design_rationale: WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST: the surface goal ('cancel my Elite Specialty package and refund what I haven't used') never names refund_amount_usd, cancellation_amount_usd, reassignment_fee_usd or sessions_delta; the agent must read pt_ext_refund's rule to learn that the unused-session count is sessions_included + bonus grants - (redeemed+late-cancelled), that the effective refund pct uplifts cancellation_refund_pct by half of any active corp enrollment's employer_discount_pct, and that a trainer-of-record mismatch must be reconciled first. This is long (bonus-loyalty and trainer-reassignment must both be discovered and resolved before refund's own compute is correct at handling time) and broad (parallel policies: pt_ext_bonus_loyalty reads membership CPARAM, pt_ext_trainer_reassignment and pt_ext_late_cancel_fee and pt_ext_refund all read corp CPARAM; history reconciliation over 4 pre-existing pt_session_redeemed rows and 1 pre-existing pt_trainer_reassigned row). SCOPE CLAIMED: this task claims the difficulty's single workflow (pt_wf_cancel_refund) as its root problem, plus the two extended policies that gate it (pt_ext_bonus_loyalty, pt_ext_trainer_reassignment) and the one nested inside it that is not itself a step (pt_ext_late_cancel_fee is nested at workflow step 1; pt_ext_refund is nested at workflow step 3). Task 1 (not yet written) will claim the remaining three policies (pt_ext_lapse_forfeit, pt_ext_archive_closed, pt_ext_purchase_pricing), which govern a disjoint set of base events (pt_package_lapsed/expired/archived/purchased/activated) never touched here. BASE-INVARIANT CARD: pt_session_redemption_eligibility (subject pt_session_redeemed) requires pt_holdings.status=active, evidenced pre-action by initial_state.pt_holdings.<PTH>.status=active — true throughout this call since nothing before step 3 (cancellation) changes status. pt_package_refund_policy's refund_requires_open_package eligibility allows status in {active, paused, closed-from-this-cancellation}; at step 3's handling time status is closed (set by step 2's cancellation the same turn), which is the closed-from-this-cancellation branch — satisfied. Its refund_within_window time eligibility anchors on pt_holdings.opened_date=2025-06-14 with duration_source=refund_window_days=10 (Elite tier), relation not_after, boundary inclusive: 2025-06-14+10d=2025-06-24; frozen_time date 2025-06-20 is not after that boundary — satisfied (a boundary case one day past 2025-06-24 would fail; a case exactly on 2025-06-24 would still pass since the boundary is inclusive). pt_specialty_membership_gating is irrelevant here (it gates purchase, not cancellation/refund) but is confirmed satisfied anyway since the membership is active at rank 4. WORLD ROW LOAD-BEARING ROLES: the 4 pre-existing pt_session_redeemed rows (ev 2025-06-15/16/17/18) are the redeemed_count history pt_ext_refund's compute sums; removing any one changes sessions_used and therefore refund_amount_usd. The 1 pre-existing pt_trainer_reassigned row (2025-06-16, trainer_name=Jordan Wu) is the authoritative evidence that pt_holdings.assigned_trainer_name='Marcus Bell' is stale (the LATEST reassignment ledger entry disagrees with the holding's own field) — this is the trainer-reconciliation prerequisite's only evidence; without this row the mismatch could not be proven and the prerequisite would already be satisfied vacuously. The active membership (Metro Multi-Club Access, personal_training_discount_pct=5) and active corp enrollment (Small Business Partner, employer_discount_pct=15) are both load-bearing cross-category holdings: removing the membership row raises pt_ext_bonus_loyalty's min_tenure from 6 back to the full 7 days, which flips tenure_met false (days_open=6 no longer clears 7) and owed to 0, so the membership CPARAM factor is genuinely load-bearing there; the percentage_elapsed proration branch of pt_ext_refund and the under_free branch of pt_ext_trainer_reassignment are each deliberately kept untriggered in this world (the required untriggered branch on each key >=6-factor computation); removing the corp row zeroes every corp-discount factor in pt_ext_late_cancel_fee, pt_ext_trainer_reassignment and pt_ext_refund, which is exactly why corp EXISTS/CPARAM is a genuine, exercised, load-bearing factor and not a decorative reference. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: every ledger row and every write carries pt_holding_id=PTH as its correlation key; there is only one PT package in this world, so no sibling-holding exclusion is needed; the trainer-reassignment fee and the refund both settle against this same PTH, never against a case-wide or customer-wide aggregate. PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root_problem=pt_wf_cancel_refund (the customer's surface request — cancel and refund). Two prerequisites, both external to the workflow's own 4 steps: (1) pt_ext_bonus_loyalty, kind=value_input, gate= the total_granted compute binding of pt_ext_refund — unresolved at frozen_time because no pt_bonus_session_granted row exists yet for PTH while eligible_tier=true and days_open(6)>=min_tenure(6) (the membership-shortened requirement; without the active membership the full 7-day requirement would not yet be met); resolved by grant_bonus_session_f02d8384; once resolved, total_granted rises from 20 to 21, moving refund_amount_usd from 970.60 to 1039.93 (the skip-sensitivity run below). (2) pt_ext_trainer_reassignment, kind=state_gate, gate= pt_holdings.assigned_trainer_name — unresolved at frozen_time because assigned_trainer_name='Marcus Bell' while the latest pt_trainer_reassigned row names 'Jordan Wu'; resolved by reassign_trainer_0e491cd1, which sets assigned_trainer_name to match. Topological order: both prerequisites are mutually independent (neither writes a field the other reads), so [bonus_loyalty, trainer_reassignment] and [trainer_reassignment, bonus_loyalty] are both valid; gold uses the former. NO_USER_HINT: user_scenario (below) never names a bonus session, a trainer reassignment, or any prerequisite; Priya only ever states her own situation, and gives her trainer's name only when asked, using the name that happens to match the ledger's own truth (Jordan Wu), not the stale holdings field she has no way of knowing about. TOOLS_DO_NOT_BLOCK: neither grant_bonus_session_f02d8384 nor reassign_trainer_0e491cd1 nor record_package_refund_4aaf76ef checks any precondition in task_tools.py — each simply looks up the holding by id and writes; an agent that calls record_package_refund_4aaf76ef before resolving either prerequisite would still get a normal confirmation string back, just with a lower, wrong refund_amount_usd and a stale trainer name, which only the terminal-hash comparison catches. STANDARD SOLUTION: locate and verify Priya; read pt_holdings, pt_events, membership_holdings, corporate_wellness_enrollments; recognize from pt_ext_bonus_loyalty's rule that a bonus session is owed (grant it); recognize from pt_ext_refund's rule that the trainer-of-record must be reconciled (reassign it); then run the workflow: log the session already attended (redeem), log the session being cancelled right now within the window (late-cancel, pt_ext_late_cancel_fee), let Priya confirm cancellation (user tool), and finally record the refund (pt_ext_refund) with the handling-time-correct amount. VERIFICATION (executed by hand against this exact seed, reproduced here): per_session_value=1499/20=74.95; after bonus (+1) and workflow (redeemed 4th=-1, late-cancelled=-1): total_granted=21, sessions_used=6, unused=15, unused_value=15*74.95=1124.25; base_pct=85, corp employer_discount_pct=15 -> uplift=7.5 -> effective_pct=92.5; refund_amount_usd=round(1124.25*0.925,2)=1039.93. late-cancel: base_fee=25, fee_after_corp=25*(1-7.5/100)=23.125, prior_late_count=0 so (0+1)<threshold(4) -> penalty=0 -> cancellation_amount_usd=round(23.125,2)=23.12 (Python banker's-adjacent float rounding of 23.125 -> 23.12, verified by running round(23.125,2) in the actual interpreter). trainer reassignment: flat_fee=30, prior_count=1, free_uses=1, under_free=(1<1)=false, fee_after_corp=30*(1-15/100)=25.5 -> reassignment_fee_usd=25.5. Skip-bonus sensitivity: with total_granted held at 20 instead of 21, unused=14, unused_value=14*74.95=1049.3, refund=round(1049.3*0.925,2)=970.60 != 1039.93, confirming the value_input edge is load-bearing. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT ONLY: reading only the published rule prose, the tool schemas and Priya's own lines (masking compute/expected/GT), the same four numbers are re-derivable: the two prerequisite rules are stated in general prose reachable from pt_ext_bonus_loyalty and pt_ext_trainer_reassignment's rule fields once rendered, the read tools return the same rows, and no second candidate action or object exists in this world — agreement confirmed.
user_scenario: Priya Anand calls in sounding a little rushed but friendly. She explains she's moving out of the metro area at the end of the month for a new job, so she needs to cancel her personal-training package and get back whatever she hasn't used yet -- she paid for a full block of sessions up front and doesn't want to lose that money since she won't be around to use them. She's fine with the representative pulling up her account and handling the cancellation and refund directly; she just wants to confirm the cancellation herself once everything is ready, since it's her package. If asked to verify who she is, she gives her mobile number, 5555550212, and, if asked for a second detail, her date of birth, 1988-04-11 (April 11th, 1988); she doesn't offer her email or photo id unless specifically asked for those instead. If asked which package she means, she says it's her Elite Specialty Coaching package -- the one with the specialty trainer, not any regular membership. If the representative asks whether she's had any sessions recently that might not be on file yet, she says yes, actually, she had a session just a couple of days ago that she doesn't think got logged. She also mentions, only if asked, that she has one more session on the calendar for tomorrow that she now has to cancel because of the move -- she won't be able to make it, and she understands there's a cancellation charge for cancelling this close to the session, which is fine. If asked who her trainer is, she says Jordan Wu -- that's who she's been working with for the last little while. She doesn't mention anything about a trainer reassignment, a bonus session, or any billing discrepancy; she doesn't know her file still lists an old trainer's name, and she has no reason to bring it up. She also doesn't ask about her club membership or her employer's wellness program; she only confirms, if asked, that yes, she believes both are still active and in good standing, since nothing has changed on either front recently. Once the representative tells her the cancellation is ready to confirm, she goes ahead and confirms it right away using her own confirmation. Once the representative tells her the refund has been recorded, she thanks them and says that's everything she needed -- she doesn't ask for anything further, doesn't request any paperwork be mailed anywhere, and doesn't raise any new topic.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: pt_ext_bonus_loyalty's write (a pt_bonus_session_granted row affecting sessions_remaining and the ledger) and pt_ext_trainer_reassignment's write (a pt_trainer_reassigned row and the assigned_trainer_name field) touch entirely disjoint fields and ledger event types; running reassignment before the bonus grant instead leaves every later count and the final refund amount identical, so both orderings are valid and gold's [bonus_loyalty, trainer_reassignment] order is not the only one.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: skipping the bonus grant leaves total_granted=20 instead of 21, unused=14 instead of 15, unused_value=1049.3 instead of 1124.25, and refund_amount_usd=970.60 instead of 1039.93 -- a changed scored parameter.

skipping the reassignment leaves pt_holdings.assigned_trainer_name at 'Marcus Bell' (never updated to 'Jordan Wu') and the gold pt_trainer_reassigned row for this call missing from the ledger entirely -- both are terminal-state differences from the gold hash, even though refund_amount_usd's arithmetic itself does not read assigned_trainer_name.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names a bonus session, a trainer reassignment, or any trainer-record mismatch; Priya's only trainer-related statement is her own trainer's name, Jordan Wu, given only when asked, and she has no reason to know or mention that pt_holdings.assigned_trainer_name still says something else.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: grant_bonus_session_f02d8384 and reassign_trainer_0e491cd1 (task_tools.py) each simply look up the holding by pt_holding_id and write, with no check of tenure, eligibility, prior grants, or trainer-name agreement; record_package_refund_4aaf76ef likewise looks up the holding and writes the stated amount with no check that either prerequisite has run, so an agent that skipped both would still receive a normal confirmation string back with the wrong refund_amount_usd.
